meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen saw a zero on his phone in the middle of class and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that, and on what basis.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Now the basis, Hale: what made you decide Owen didn't write his own essay?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Turn the screen so I can read it myself, Hale, and tell me who else has seen it. Pasting into a document proves where it was pasted, not who wrote it.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm searching it now. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, Hale, and a wrong line is not a finding of anything. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

That's your own procedure 4.4, so I'll hold you to every word of it. Thursday at 8:15, no other students in the room, and I want it in an email tonight that nothing goes on his file, whatever the vice-principal thinks of him. I'll agree to that to put this behind him, not because Owen did anything.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, and that if it holds up the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I still require written confirmation that nothing goes on his file and that no other students will be in the room. I expect that email from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position, agreeing to the supervised rewrite Thursday morning, and she still wants a written promise that nothing goes on Owen's file and that no other students are present.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times, because it was specific, dated, tied to Owen's own document, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing, because you owned the early zero in one sentence and never leaned on the detector or attacked Owen.
Try next time: When she asked who else had seen the version history, answer that directly before moving on to your next piece of evidence.
